Definition: Beth-Shean or Beth-Shan, a place in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Beth-Shean means house of ease, and it is named where Israel's story turns darkest. Joshua 17:11 gives it to Manasseh, though the Canaanites still held it, and 1 Samuel 31:10 says the Philistines fastened Saul's body to the wall of Beth-shan after Gilboa. Then 1 Samuel 31:12 tells how the valiant men of Jabesh went all night and took the body of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-shan.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Beth-shean shows both sides of the same wall: shame fastened to it, and loyalty that came in the night to take it down.
